text: In the Hill equation v = Vmax[S]^n / (K0.5^n + [S]^n), what does a Hill coefficient n > 1 indicate?
choices: Negative cooperativity, producing a more graded response
Strictly hyperbolic Michaelis-Menten kinetics with no cooperativity
Positive cooperativity, producing an ultrasensitive, switch-like response
Zero-order kinetics, independent of substrate concentration
explanation: A Hill coefficient n > 1 indicates positive cooperativity: binding of one ligand increases the affinity for subsequent ligands, producing a steep, switch-like (ultrasensitive) response curve. Negative cooperativity would give n < 1, ordinary Michaelis-Menten hyperbolic kinetics corresponds to n = 1, and zero-order kinetics describes a rate that is independent of substrate concentration, an unrelated kinetic regime.
